declaration: Windows power scheme set to High Performance; standby, monitor and hibernate timeouts all 0 on AC; machine on AC throughout the collection.

environment_variable.name: AEP_HARNESS_SUSPEND_DISABLED
environment_variable.effect: Recorded into every run config as suspend_disabled_declared=true. Amendment E5's gate in experiments/analyze.py admits a run to absolute-timing aggregates only when it is declared AND no suspension was detected in its own settling polls.

independently_measured.tool: powercfg, run on the Windows host at declaration time
independently_measured.note: The measurement corroborates the declaration; it does not replace it. E5 exists because a host that merely was not idle long enough to suspend is indistinguishable from one that cannot.

residual_risks_not_covered_by_the_declar: On battery the same scheme sets STANDBYIDLE and VIDEOIDLE to 240s; the protection is conditional on remaining on AC, which the declaration asserts.
The host reports one battery and supports S0 Low Power Idle, so it is a laptop. Lid-close action was not verifiable from powercfg output and is not covered by the timeout settings.
The declaration cannot be verified retrospectively. analyze.py's second gate, suspension_detected, is what catches a host that suspended anyway.

supersedes.reason: Collection started 2026-08-13T10:20:28Z without the declaration; every run there records suspend_disabled_declared=false. Restarted rather than resumed, so that all 432 runs carry the same declaration and the timing denominator equals the count denominator.
